c1443.summary: Tyagaraja urges the listener to chant Shiva's name and live a disciplined life of worship and good company.
m: Can't you say 'Shiva, Shiva, Shiva'?
Can't you crush the troubles and fears of worldly life?
Cutting off desire and the rest, shunning others' wives and others' wealth,
leaving behind base ways, worshipping with bilva leaves with great discipline,
seeking the company of good people, regarding them as lords of the three worlds,
casting off shame and the like, worshipping Him in the lotus of your own heart,
praising the Agamas, giving up idle talk,
thriving among devotees, holding Him praised by Tyagaraja in your thoughts — (say Shiva).

c1280.summary: A Sanskrit hymn saluting Rama of most beautiful form, with a long garland of his qualities.
m: I salute Rama, of most beautiful form,
with teeth like jasmine buds, moon to the lilies of his dear ones, flawless, radiant as countless Manmathas,
purifier of the fallen, protector of the worlds, abode of all the Vedas, of auspicious face,
the life of great ascetics, protector of the elephant king, crusher of the demons' pride, saviour of the humble,
dark as a fresh blade of durva grass, delighting the hosts of gods, protector of the gods who bow, of wondrous play,
death to the fear of worldly life, loving to his devotees, auspicious, non-dual, pure, in radiant golden garments,
moving through the Agamas, support of all worlds, dear to Brahma, hero of heroes,
destroyer of attachment and the like, Raghava, generous, moving in Tyagaraja's heart, ocean of compassion.

c2832.summary: A song of auspiciousness (shobhanam) asking Rama for protection.
m: Auspiciousness!
Your radiant face outshining the moon, desired by the earth, terror to the proud — protect me, Sri Rama.
Delight of Janaka's daughter, who humbled Parashurama's pride, fire to the sins of those who bow, refuge of sages — protect me.
Who cut the noose of delusion, radiant as ten million moons, Lord and master of all — protect me, destroyer of sin.
Praised by noble Tyagaraja, father of the lotus-born, supremely auspicious — protect me, O one of holy deeds.

c2896.summary: Sung at Tirupati when the curtain was drawn before the deity: Tyagaraja asks Venkateshvara to remove the curtain of jealousy within him.
m: Won't you remove the curtain within me, Tirupati Venkataramana — the curtain of jealousy?
O Supreme Person, it is driving away dharma and the other aims, even liberation, from within me.
It is like a hungry fish caught on the hook;
like a screen fallen before a clear lamp, hiding its light;
like a fly falling (into the food) while one eats contentedly;
when I meditate on Hari, my mind wanders off to an outcast's street;
it is like deer coming and getting caught, not knowing it is a net.
Quickly — (remove) the curtain of pride and jealousy from Tyagaraja, who follows your path.

c2342.summary: What power do the planets have? Rama's grace is the only power.
m: What is the power of the planets? Sri Rama's grace alone is power.
What power do the planets have over those who meditate on His radiant form?
The torments of the nine planets and the five great sins — for one who worships Hari, subduer
of the fierce enemies like desire — (are nothing) for Tyagaraja and the foremost of connoisseurs.

c2873.summary: A prayer to Rama, life of the good, adorned with virtues.
m: Rama, life of the good, adorned with virtues,
worshipped by Shiva who wears serpents, protector of the wise, revered by Hanuman, sandal-paste to those who seek refuge, son of Dasharatha — protect me.
Lovely-eyed, consort of Lakshmi, of beautiful form, of saving name and noble deeds, son of Dasharatha,
slayer of Taraka and others, protector of dharma — save me, Raghuvara, pure one, praised by Tyagaraja.

c1278.summary: A celebration of the grandeur of the wedding of Sita and Rama, with a garland of Rama's epithets.
m: The grandeur of Sita's wedding! The grandeur of Rama's wedding!
Worthy of Hanuman's praise, of holy deeds, with sun, moon and wind as eyes, of lovely form,
protector of devotees, bearer of arrows, who in play grants worldly joy and liberation, protector of Brahmins,
terror to the wicked, wholly fulfilled, dark-hued, delight of the world, dweller in Saketa,
support of all worlds, peerless in battle, far from the proud, steadfast hero,
who roams the Vedas and Agamas, of matchless form, who held up the mountain, support of the worlds that bow,
whose songs Shiva praises, the ship across the ocean of worldly life, born in the Solar race, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2318.summary: Tyagaraja confesses his misspent life and wonders how Rama will ever protect him.
m: I don't know how you will protect me, O Ramayya, my only refuge.
Alas, my story is harsh to the ear.
I roamed and fed like a barren bull; I praised born misers to fill my belly;
keeping company with the wicked and doing evil deeds — how will you, in compassion, (save) Tyagaraja who made such a mess?

c2597.summary: Am I not your servant? Tyagaraja asks Rama to show him love and guide him to the shore.
m: Show your love for me — am I not your servant, Sri Rama?
Whose feet are worshipped by Sanaka and the hosts of yogis, dweller in Saketa, nurturer of true devotees,
I have long trusted you as mother, father, guru and God;
as I struggle, why don't you show me the shore? Protector of Tyagaraja, of virtuous nature.

c2914.summary: On those who boast of mastering raga and laya without knowing nada, the divine form of Om.
m: They boast that they are masters of noble raga and laya, Sri Rama,
without knowing in their hearts the distinctions of svara, jati and murchana.
Nada born of God, the divine form of the Pranava —
how such men, who never thirst for it, deceive! O Rama praised by Tyagaraja.

c1083.summary: Rama tried every means — conciliation, gifts, division and punishment — with Ravana; who is a God like him?
m: Who is a God like you, skilled in conciliation, gifts, division and punishment? Protect me.
When Ravana, who claimed to be foremost among Shiva's devotees, would not understand,
how many words of good counsel you spoke; you even offered 'Ayodhya is yours';
you made his brother, who bowed to you, king, and when Ravana did not yield you slew him — O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2309.summary: How much must I plead? Why this obstinacy, Rama?
m: How much should I plead, O Raghava? Why this obstinacy, O Raghava?
How hard is it to end my worry? O inner Self, if you don't come near me —
rejoicing, thinking that the bliss of seeing you in my heart is the highest,
I trusted you so deeply — will you be a mere bystander? O emperor, praised by Sri Tyagaraja.

c2933.summary: Tyagaraja bows to the great masters of music, divine and human, who know the secret of nada.
m: I bow to the masters of music —
the masters of the Sama Veda joyfully made by Shankara, (who know) the seven svaras that are nada itself:
Lakshmi, Gauri, Sarasvati, Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Narada, Indra, Bharata, Kashyapa,
Chandikeshvara, Anjaneya, Guha, Ganesha, Markandeya, Agastya, Tumburu, the noble Someshvara,
Sharngadeva, Nandi and the foremost ones, revered by Tyagaraja, who know the secret of the ocean of bliss.

c1047.summary: Tyagaraja will worship Rama's feet with tulasi leaves; he has offered every other flower already.
m: With tulasi leaves I will joyfully worship
again and again, for ever, the feet of the Supreme Self.
Lotus, punnaga, champaka, patala, kuruvaka, oleander, jasmine and the fragrant royal flowers —
these of the earth I have offered once; (now with tulasi I worship) the righteous Sri Rama of Saketa, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2560.summary: Come, let me see you, Rama — steady as Mount Meru, graceful in gait, radiant in beauty.
m: Steady as Mount Meru, giver of boons, hero of the Raghus — come, let me see you, great one:
your graceful gait, essence of all essences, your rain-cloud radiance and splendour, great one;
the charm of your curls, the line of your tilaka, your face lovely with gleaming cheeks,
the golden ornaments shining on your neck — crusher of the wicked, worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c2451.summary: Without the power to still the mind, outward rituals — worship, holy baths, sacrifices, penance — are useless.
m: If one has no power to still the mind, what will worship with sweet bells and flowers achieve?
If one drowns oneself in arrogance, how can the Kaveri or the Ganga save him?
If the sacrificer longs after beautiful women, does he become worthy of heaven?
If one full of desire and anger does penance, will it protect him? — O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2667.summary: Tyagaraja declares that he worships Rama alone and will beg no other.
m: I am one who worships only you.
O you who recline on the serpent, I cannot beg others.
Giver of the joy of bathing, japa, penance, yoga, meditation and samadhi,
Lord of Sita, protector of all worlds, praised by Tyagaraja.

c1020.summary: Tyagaraja tells his mind the secret of Rama's compassion: he took human form to save those lost in ritual and worldly life.
m: Won't you listen to my plea? I will tell you the whole secret, O mind.
I know the compassionate inner heart of great Ramachandra:
when people drawn to ritualism wandered in the dense forest of worldly life and suffered,
seeing them, he took human form and appeared that very day — so says Tyagaraja.

c1596.summary: Tyagaraja has wholly trusted Rama's feet as his refuge, and asks to be taken in, however it may be.
m: I am one who has wholly trusted that your feet are my refuge, Rama.
Lord of all, known through the Vedas and Vedanta, Rama,
my sinful deeds are many; I cannot bear the troubles here;
in whatever way, take me as your own, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c1002.summary: Is it a burden to protect me? You hold millions of universes and lifted mountains for others.
m: Is it a burden to protect me, Raghurama — you who have become the whole world — just me alone?
Sri Vasudeva, do you not hold millions of universes in your belly?
In the ocean of milk, compassionately, for the gods (you bore the mountain); and besides, for the gopis'
sake, did you not lift a mountain? O compassionate one, (is protecting) Tyagaraja (a burden)?

c1440.summary: Why blame Rama? Everything comes according to one's own karma, dharma and mind.
m: Why blame you, lotus-eyed Sri Rama?
Why lash out at my parents or anyone else?
Events unfold according to karma; God protects according to dharma;
fulfilment comes according to the mind; enjoyment comes according to one's merit.
(So it was shown) to Tyagaraja, who praised you, the embodiment of goodness, and knew the truth.

c2553.summary: Tyagaraja cries out again and again; Rama rushed for the elephant, Dhruva and Prahlada — why not for him?
m: Though I cry out to you again and again, compassion does not enter your heart.
What made you rush at the elephant's cry, O indweller of all?
I have heard how compassionately you stood before Dhruva; for the son of the gods' enemy (Prahlada)
you became the man-lion without warning; and the greatness of saving the forest-dweller who had forgotten (you) —
tell me, O one praised by Tyagaraja, shining on earth; I can no longer bear just hearing (such stories).

c2848.summary: A prayer to Rama's feet, which released Ahalya from the curse: bless me the same way.
m: O feet of Sri Rama, your grace is enough — come into my heart,
(you feet) worshipped by Brahma, Sanaka, Sanandana, Indra, Narada and all the others.
On the path, (Ahalya) had become stone, unable to bear her suffering, shedding tears constantly;
valiant one, seeing Ahalya you saved her — in that way make me blessed too, O fortune of Tyagaraja.

c2300.summary: How long will you stay silent, Rama? Is there no one to ask you why?
m: How long will you stay silent here? Is there no one to question you, Sri Rama?
Did you not rule Saketa for a while? Did you not fulfil the sages' wishes?
Did you not heed your wife's words and protect countless true devotees? Is not protecting the wise
your very creed? Has not Sri Tyagaraja, who always praises you, trusted you?
